12:1.sourceText: Κατ’ ἐκεῖνον δὲ τὸν καιρὸν ἐπέβαλεν Ἡρῴδης ὁ βασιλεὺς τὰς χεῖρας κακῶσαί τινας τῶν ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας.
12:1.targetText: And about that time, Herod the king put forth his hands to do evil to certain of those of the Assembly,

groups.note: The actual definite hands belong to the putting-forth subject Herod; English marks the same agent-owned body part with his, without an additional Greek possessive.
The actual κακῶσαι is one harm-or-mistreat verb, rendered to do evil to; there are not separate printed do and evil words.

unmappedSource.reason: The article with that time is not separately expressed.

12:2.sourceText: ἀνεῖλεν δὲ Ἰάκωβον τὸν ἀδελφὸν Ἰωάνου μαχαίρῃ.
12:2.targetText: and he killed James, the brother of John, with the sword,

groups.note: The dative sword noun gives the instrument, rendered with the sword without a separate Greek with preposition.

12:3.sourceText: ἰδὼν δὲ ὅτι ἀρεστόν ἐστιν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις προσέθετο συλλαβεῖν καὶ Πέτρον, ἦσαν δὲ ἡμέραι τῶν ἀζύμων,
12:3.targetText: and having seen that it is pleasing to the Jews, he added to lay hold of Peter also—and they were the days of the Unleavened [Bread]—

groups.note: The actual substantival unleavened plural designates the bread or festival, rendered Unleavened [Bread]. Its source remains ἄζυμος, not an additional ἄρτος bread noun. Primary lexical entry specifically includes Acts12:3: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/azymos .

12:4.sourceText: ὃν καὶ πιάσας ἔθετο εἰς φυλακήν, παραδοὺς τέσσαρσιν τετραδίοις στρατιωτῶν φυλάσσειν αὐτόν, βουλόμενος μετὰ τὸ πάσχα ἀναγαγεῖν αὐτὸν τῷ λαῷ.
12:4.targetText: whom also having seized, he put in prison, having delivered [him] to four squads of four soldiers to guard him, intending to bring him forth to the people after the Passover.

groups.note: The actual relative whom is the same Peter seized, put in prison, and delivered for guarding; English repeats him with the immediate delivering predicate. No additional object pronoun is invented there; the later guarding and bringing objects have their own written pronouns.

The dative τετραδίοις names squads of four; the four within that noun is part of its lexical meaning, separate from the preceding actual numeral τέσσαρσιν counting four squads. English to expresses the dative recipient construction.

12:5.sourceText: ὁ μὲν οὖν Πέτρος ἐτηρεῖτο ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ· προσευχὴ δὲ ἦν ἐκτενῶς γινομένη ὑπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν περὶ αὐτοῦ.
12:5.targetText: Peter, therefore, indeed, was kept in the prison, and fervent prayer was being made by the Assembly to God for him,

groups.note: The actual ἐκτενῶς is an adverb, fervently; English recasts it as adjectival fervent modifying prayer, not a source adjective.
The actual γινομένη is a middle-form becoming/occurring participle, rendered being made with prayer; it is not a printed passive ποιέω form.

unmappedSource.reason: The articles before Peter and God are not separately expressed.

12:6.sourceText: Ὅτε δὲ ἤμελλεν προαγαγεῖν αὐτὸν ὁ Ἡρῴδης, τῇ νυκτὶ ἐκείνῃ ἦν ὁ Πέτρος κοιμώμενος μεταξὺ δύο στρατιωτῶν δεδεμένος ἁλύσεσιν δυσίν, φύλακές τε πρὸ τῆς θύρας ἐτήρουν τὴν φυλακήν.
12:6.targetText: and when Herod was about to bring him forth, the same night was Peter sleeping between two soldiers, having been bound with two chains, guards were also keeping the prison before the door,

groups.note: The actual demonstrative ἐκείνῃ is that; English same identifies this same specified night without a printed αὐτός adjective for same.
The dative chains noun expresses the binding instrument, rendered with two chains; with is not a separately printed Greek preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The articles before Herod and Peter are not separately expressed.

12:7.sourceText: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄγγελος Κυρίου ἐπέστη, καὶ φῶς ἔλαμψεν ἐν τῷ οἰκήματι· πατάξας δὲ τὴν πλευρὰν τοῦ Πέτρου ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν λέγων Ἀνάστα ἐν τάχει. καὶ ἐξέπεσαν αὐτοῦ αἱ ἁλύσεις ἐκ τῶν χειρῶν.
12:7.targetText: and behold, a messenger of the LORD stood by, and a light shone in the buildings, and having struck Peter on the side, he raised him up, saying, “Rise in haste,” and his chains fell from off [his] hands.

groups.note: The actual οἰκήματι is a singular dative dwelling or room noun in both pinned analyses; English buildings is plural wording for that head. The pinned TR also has the singular form, not a different plural source reading.

The actual accusative side phrase is the striking object, with Peter as its genitive owner; English recasts the same body-part construction as struck Peter on the side. The English on comes from this role recast, not a separately printed preposition.
The actual Πέτρου is genitive, the owner of the struck side, recast as English Peter after struck; this is not a source accusative name.

The one actual genitive αὐτοῦ identifies Peter as owner in the chains/hands scene. English uses his for the chains and repeats bracketed his for the same person’s hands; no second possessive source token is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Peter and the articles under the English possessive chains/hands expressions are not separately expressed.

12:8.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ ἄγγελος πρὸς αὐτόν Ζῶσαι καὶ ὑπόδησαι τὰ σανδάλιά σου. ἐποίησεν δὲ οὕτως. καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Περιβαλοῦ τὸ ἱμάτιόν σου καὶ ἀκολούθει μοι.
12:8.targetText: The messenger also said to him, “Gird yourself, and bind on your sandals”; and he did so; and he says to him, “Cast your garment around and follow me”;

groups.note: The middle imperative Ζῶσαι encodes the subject’s self-girding; English yourself expresses this middle action without a separately written reflexive pronoun.

unmappedSource.reason: The articles in the possessive sandals and garment phrases are not separately expressed.

12:9.sourceText: καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἠκολούθει, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδει ὅτι ἀληθές ἐστιν τὸ γινόμενον διὰ τοῦ ἀγγέλου, ἐδόκει δὲ ὅραμα βλέπειν.
12:9.targetText: and having gone forth, he was following him, and he did not know that it is true that which is done through the messenger, and was thinking he saw a vision,

groups.note: The actual γινόμενον is a present middle-form happening/becoming participle, rendered is done; no source passive doing verb is substituted.

The actual genitive ἀγγέλου names the messenger as agent after through. That same immediately followed/acting messenger supplies the earlier English him as following recipient; one actual noun identity is shared across those two roles, not converted into an αὐτός pronoun. The pinned TR independently prints a recipient αὐτῷ with following, absent from N1904.
The actual βλέπειν is a present active infinitive complement of thinking; English he saw recasts that same seeing predicate as a finite past content clause.

12:10.sourceText: διελθόντες δὲ πρώτην φυλακὴν καὶ δευτέραν ἦλθαν ἐπὶ τὴν πύλην τὴν σιδηρᾶν τὴν φέρουσαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν, ἥτις αὐτομάτη ἠνοίγη αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐξελθόντες προῆλθον ῥύμην μίαν, καὶ εὐθέως ἀπέστη ὁ ἄγγελος ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ.
12:10.targetText: and having passed through a first ward, and a second, they came to the iron gate that is leading into the city, which opened to them of its own accord, and having gone forth, they went on through one street, and immediately the messenger departed from him.

groups.note: The substantival ordinal δευτέραν expresses the second ward with the noun understood from the first ward; English a second likewise does not require an additional source ward noun.
The actual αὐτομάτη is a feminine adjective modifying the gate, rendered of its own accord; it is one word, not a separately printed possessive pronoun and accord noun.

The actual accusative street noun expresses the traversed path with went on, rendered through one street; through is supplied by that path construction rather than a separately written Greek preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The repeated article introducing the iron modifier has no separate English word.

12:11.sourceText: καὶ ὁ Πέτρος ἐν ἑαυτῷ γενόμενος εἶπεν Νῦν οἶδα ἀληθῶς ὅτι ἐξαπέστειλεν ὁ Κύριος τὸν ἄγγελον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξείλατό με ἐκ χειρὸς Ἡρῴδου καὶ πάσης τῆς προσδοκίας τοῦ λαοῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων.
12:11.targetText: And Peter having come to himself, said, “Now I have known of a truth that the LORD sent forth His messenger, and delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and all the expectation of the people of the Jews”;

groups.note: The actual becoming-in-himself construction names the return to awareness, rendered having come to himself; it is not a separately printed ἔρχομαι coming verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The articles before Peter and the possessive messenger phrase are not separately expressed.

12:12.sourceText: συνιδών τε ἦλθεν ἐπὶ τὴν οἰκίαν τῆς Μαρίας τῆς μητρὸς Ἰωάνου τοῦ ἐπικαλουμένου Μάρκου, οὗ ἦσαν ἱκανοὶ συνηθροισμένοι καὶ προσευχόμενοι.
12:12.targetText: also, having considered, he came to the house of Mary, the mother of John, who is surnamed Mark, where there were many thronged together and praying.

12:13.sourceText: κρούσαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ τὴν θύραν τοῦ πυλῶνος προσῆλθεν παιδίσκη ὑπακοῦσαι ὀνόματι Ῥόδη,
12:13.targetText: And Peter having knocked at the door of the porch, there came a girl to listen, by name Rhoda,

groups.note: The actual accusative door phrase is the knocking object, rendered at the door in the English construction; at is not a separately written Greek preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 has the personal genitive αὐτοῦ as subject of the knocking genitive absolute. The pinned TR names τοῦ Πέτρου, Peter, instead; the differing printed personal expressions remain unpaired.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR explicitly names Peter in the knocking clause, whereas N1904 has αὐτοῦ, him; no Peter noun is invented for that source pronoun.

12:14.sourceText: καὶ ἐπιγνοῦσα τὴν φωνὴν τοῦ Πέτρου ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς οὐκ ἤνοιξεν τὸν πυλῶνα, εἰσδραμοῦσα δὲ ἀπήγγειλεν ἑστάναι τὸν Πέτρον πρὸ τοῦ πυλῶνος.
12:14.targetText: and having known the voice of Peter, from the joy she did not open the porch, but having run in, told of the standing of Peter before the porch,

groups.note: The actual perfect infinitive ἑστάναι is the reported standing predicate, recast as the English verbal noun of the standing; there is no separate written standing noun or of preposition.
The actual article and Peter are accusative, the personal subject of the reported standing infinitive; English expresses that same standing person as of Peter under its nominal recast.

12:15.sourceText: οἱ δὲ πρὸς αὐτὴν εἶπαν Μαίνῃ. ἡ δὲ διϊσχυρίζετο οὕτως ἔχειν. οἱ δὲ ἔλεγον Ὁ ἄγγελός ἐστιν αὐτοῦ.
12:15.targetText: and they said to her, “You are mad”; and she was confidently affirming [it] to be so, and they said, “It is his messenger”;

groups.note: The actual Μαίνῃ is a finite madness verb, be out of one’s mind; English You are mad expands that one predicate rather than an unwritten copula plus a source adjective.
The actual ἔχειν with οὕτως is the expression for the situation holding so, rendered to be so; it is an infinitive, not a source finite be verb.
The actual finite ἐστιν anchors It is in the English identification recast. Greek has the definite messenger and a genitive possessor; no independently printed neuter it pronoun is asserted.

unmappedSource.reason: The article defining the messenger has no separate English the under the possessive predicate recast.

unmappedTarget.reason: The object of the reported assertion is supplied as bracketed it; there is no independent Greek object pronoun for that proposition.

12:16.sourceText: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἐπέμενεν κρούων· ἀνοίξαντες δὲ εἶδαν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐξέστησαν.
12:16.targetText: and Peter was continuing knocking, and having opened, they saw him, and were astonished,

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Peter is not separately expressed.

12:17.sourceText: κατασείσας δὲ αὐτοῖς τῇ χειρὶ σιγᾶν διηγήσατο αὐτοῖς πῶς ὁ Κύριος αὐτὸν ἐξήγαγεν ἐκ τῆς φυλακῆς, εἶπέν τε Ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰακώβῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ταῦτα. καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἐπορεύθη εἰς ἕτερον τόπον.
12:17.targetText: and having beckoned to them with the hand to be silent, he declared to them how the LORD brought him out of the prison, and he said, “Declare these things to James and to the brothers”; and having gone forth, he went on to another place.

12:18.sourceText: Γενομένης δὲ ἡμέρας ἦν τάραχος οὐκ ὀλίγος ἐν τοῖς στρατιώταις, τί ἄρα ὁ Πέτρος ἐγένετο.
12:18.targetText: And day having come, there was not a little stir among the soldiers what then was become of Peter,

groups.note: The actual Peter is nominative, the person in the what-became question; English uses of Peter with was become, retaining the same person without a separately printed of preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Peter is not separately expressed under the English of Peter construction.

12:19.sourceText: Ἡρῴδης δὲ ἐπιζητήσας αὐτὸν καὶ μὴ εὑρὼν, ἀνακρίνας τοὺς φύλακας ἐκέλευσεν ἀπαχθῆναι, καὶ κατελθὼν ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας εἰς Καισάριαν διέτριβεν.
12:19.targetText: and Herod having sought for him, and having not found, having examined the guards, commanded [them] to be led away to punishment, and having gone down from Judea to Caesarea, he was abiding [there].

groups.note: The actual guards are the same immediate examined people ordered to be led away; English resumes this actual noun with bracketed them, without an additional source pronoun.

targetPhrases.text: to be led away to punishment

groups.note: The actual passive infinitive ἀπαχθῆναι is lead away, used here for leading away to execution or punishment; the English explanatory to punishment is not a separately printed noun. Primary lexical entry specifically cites Acts12:19: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/apago .

The one actual Caesarea name supplies the destination and the location of the immediate abiding; English repeats that known place as bracketed there, without an additional source place-adverb identity.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Judea is not separately expressed.

12:20.sourceText: Ἦν δὲ θυμομαχῶν Τυρίοις καὶ Σιδωνίοις· ὁμοθυμαδὸν δὲ παρῆσαν πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ πείσαντες Βλάστον τὸν ἐπὶ τοῦ κοιτῶνος τοῦ βασιλέως ᾐτοῦντο εἰρήνην, διὰ τὸ τρέφεσθαι αὐτῶν τὴν χώραν ἀπὸ τῆς βασιλικῆς.
12:20.targetText: And Herod was highly displeased with the Tyrians and Sidonians, and with one accord they came to him, and having made a friend of Blastus, who [is] over the bed-chambers of the king, they were asking peace, because of their country being nourished from the king’s;

groups.note: The dative Tyrians expresses the people toward whom the displeasure is directed, rendered with the Tyrians; with is not a separately written Greek preposition.
The actual ὁμοθυμαδόν is one unanimity adverb, rendered with one accord; neither one nor accord is a separately printed source word.

The actual πείσαντες is a persuading or winning-over participle, expressed idiomatically as having made a friend of. It does not contain a separately printed friend noun or making verb. Primary lexical entry cites the winning-over sense at Acts12:20: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/peitho .
The actual κοιτῶνος is a singular genitive bedroom/chamber noun in both pinned analyses; English bed-chambers is plural wording, not a different printed Greek plural.
The actual article and βασιλικῆς are a substantival royal adjective with the country understood, rendered the king’s. This is not a second printed βασιλεύς king noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The articular nourishing infinitive and the article under their country are not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR explicitly names Herod as the angry subject; pinned N1904 has an understood subject without this name.
The who-over-the-chamber modifier has no written be verb; English supplies bracketed is.

12:21.sourceText: τακτῇ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἐνδυσάμενος ἐσθῆτα βασιλικὴν καθίσας ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἐδημηγόρει πρὸς αὐτούς·
12:21.targetText: and on a set day, Herod having clothed himself in kingly clothing, and having sat down on the judgment seat, was making an oration to them,

groups.note: The actual dative day expresses the time, rendered on a set day without a separately printed on preposition.

The actual middle clothing participle describes the subject clothing himself; English himself and in express that middle action and its garment complement without separate printed reflexive/preposition words.

unmappedSource.reason: The article before Herod is not separately expressed.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR has an additional καί before the sitting participle, absent from N1904.

12:22.sourceText: ὁ δὲ δῆμος ἐπεφώνει Θεοῦ φωνὴ καὶ οὐκ ἀνθρώπου.
12:22.targetText: and the populace were shouting, “The voice of a god, and not of a man!”

12:23.sourceText: παραχρῆμα δὲ ἐπάταξεν αὐτὸν ἄγγελος Κυρίου ἀνθ’ ὧν οὐκ ἔδωκεν τὴν δόξαν τῷ Θεῷ, καὶ γενόμενος σκωληκόβρωτος ἐξέψυξεν.
12:23.targetText: And immediately a messenger of the LORD struck him in return for that he did not give the glory to God, and having been eaten of worms, he expired.

groups.note: The actual ἀνθ᾽ ὧν preposition-relative expression gives the stated reason, rendered in return for that; this is not four separate Greek words corresponding to those four English words.

The actual γενόμενος is a becoming participle, while σκωληκόβρωτος is a worm-eaten compound adjective. English having been eaten of worms recasts that participle-plus-adjective construction; no printed passive eating verb is invented.

12:24.sourceText: Ὁ δὲ λόγος τοῦ Κυρίου ηὔξανεν καὶ ἐπληθύνετο.
12:24.targetText: And the word of God grew and multiplied,

unmappedSource.reason: The pinned N1904 has τοῦ Κυρίου, of the Lord, while the pinned TR has τοῦ θεοῦ, of God. The whole differing genitive named expression remains unpaired.

unmappedTarget.reason: The English follows pinned TR τοῦ θεοῦ instead of N1904 τοῦ Κυρίου; no detached of is assigned to an unlike source head.

12:25.sourceText: Βαρνάβας δὲ καὶ Σαῦλος ὑπέστρεψαν, ἐξ Ἱερουσαλὴμ, πληρώσαντες τὴν διακονίαν, συνπαραλαβόντες Ἰωάνην τὸν ἐπικληθέντα Μάρκον.
12:25.targetText: and Barnabas and Saul turned back out of Jerusalem, having fulfilled the ministry, having also taken John with [them], who was surnamed Mark.

groups.note: The actual coordinated Barnabas and Saul are the agents of returning and taking John along. English resumes that same written pair with bracketed them after with; one pair of actual named identities is retained without inventing an additional pronoun.
The actual συνπαραλαβόντες is a single taking-along-with verb, expressed as having taken ... with; with is part of its companion-taking meaning rather than a separately printed preposition.

unmappedTarget.reason: The pinned TR has an additional καί before taking along; N1904 has no separate additive coordinator there.
